title: State Auto Insurance Compliance Explained: Proof of Insurance, RV Rules, SR-22 Filings & State Programs in California and Florida
description: What California and Florida actually require: minimum limits, proof of insurance, RV rules, SR-22 and FR-44 filings, real state programs, and the ads that only pretend to be one.
author: Insurance Bhaiya Research Desk
keyTakeaways: California's minimum liability limits rose to 30/60/15 ($30,000 per person, $60,000 per accident, $15,000 property damage) on January 1, 2025. Read the full breakdown in our [California evidence of liability insurance guide](/learn/california-evidence-of-liability-insurance/).

Florida requires only $10,000 Personal Injury Protection and $10,000 Property Damage Liability for most drivers, and that coverage must stay continuous for the whole registration period, even if the car never moves.

A 'Florida compliant drivers program' is not a state agency program. The real discounts come from the state-approved mature driver course, safe-driver rating and telematics. See [what the Florida compliant drivers program really is](/learn/florida-compliant-drivers-program/).

Motorhomes in California must carry the same 30/60/15 liability as a car; towable trailers have no stand-alone mandate. Details in our [California RV insurance guide](/learn/california-rv-insurance/).
SR-22 and FR-44 are filings, not policy types. An FR-44 forces Florida DUI offenders to carry 100/300/50 for at least three years. Compare them in [SR-22 vs FR-44](/qa/sr22-vs-fr44-difference/).

faqs.question: What is the minimum car insurance required in California in 2026?
faqs.answer: Liability limits of $30,000 per person and $60,000 per accident for bodily injury, plus $15,000 for property damage. These 30/60/15 limits took effect January 1, 2025. Full details are in our [California evidence of liability insurance](/learn/california-evidence-of-liability-insurance/) guide.

faqs.question: Does Florida require bodily injury liability insurance?
faqs.answer: Not for most drivers. Florida requires $10,000 in Personal Injury Protection and $10,000 in Property Damage Liability. Bodily injury liability becomes mandatory through an SR-22 or FR-44 filing after certain violations, explained in [SR-22 vs FR-44](/qa/sr22-vs-fr44-difference/).

faqs.question: Is the Florida compliant drivers program a government program?
faqs.answer: No. No Florida state agency operates a program by that name; it is a marketing phrase used by lead-generation websites. Real discounts come from the state-approved mature driver course and insurer safe-driver programs, covered in our [Florida compliant drivers program](/learn/florida-compliant-drivers-program/) guide.

faqs.question: Do I need insurance on a travel trailer in California?
faqs.answer: California does not require separate insurance on a towable trailer. Your tow vehicle's liability usually extends to it while hitched, but damage to the trailer itself is only covered if you buy physical damage coverage. See our [California RV insurance guide](/learn/california-rv-insurance/).

content.text: Most drivers think about car insurance as a price. The state thinks about it as a compliance record. California and Florida both run electronic systems that match every registered vehicle against an active policy, and when the two don't line up, the consequence isn't a higher premium. It is a suspended registration, a suspended license, a reinstatement fee, and in some cases a multi-year filing requirement that follows you to every insurer you call. This hub covers the compliance side of auto insurance in the two states our readers ask about most: what the law requires, how you prove it, how recreational vehicles fit in, which state programs are real, and which ones are marketing wearing a government costume.
Compliance Is Three Separate Things
When a state says you must be 'insured', it is actually checking three different obligations. Mixing them up is how people end up suspended while holding a perfectly valid policy.

items: **Carrying the minimum coverage.** Your policy's limits must meet the state floor. In California that floor changed in 2025, so a policy written years ago at the old limits had to be updated at renewal.

**Proving it on demand.** Police, the DMV and the other driver after a crash can all ask for evidence. California calls this 'evidence of financial responsibility' and accepts a short list of forms, which we walk through in our [California evidence of liability insurance guide](/learn/california-evidence-of-liability-insurance/).

**Keeping it continuous.** Both states receive electronic reports from insurers. A cancellation or non-payment lapse is reported automatically, and the state acts on the gap whether or not you were driving during it.

content.text: California vs Florida: The Minimums Side by Side

The two states take opposite approaches. California is a fault state that mandates bodily injury liability. Florida is a no-fault state that mandates [Personal Injury Protection](/glossary/personal-injury-protection/) for your own injuries and property damage liability, but no bodily injury liability for most drivers.

content.title: Minimum Is a Legal Floor, Not a Recommendation
content.text: A $15,000 property damage limit will not replace most new cars, and $30,000 per person rarely covers a serious injury. Anything above your limit becomes a personal debt. Before you settle on state minimums, model your exposure with the [Car Insurance Calculator](/car-insurance-calculator/) and read [what happens if you crash without insurance](/qa/what-happens-if-you-crash-without-insurance/) to see how quickly an uncovered judgment grows.

Beyond California and Florida, state insurance frameworks vary across the country. See our detailed breakdown of [is Michigan a no-fault state](/qa/is-michigan-a-no-fault-state/) to understand its unique medical PIP tiers, compare choice systems in [full tort vs limited tort](/compare/full-tort-vs-limited-tort/) states like Pennsylvania and New Jersey, and review how cross-border coverage works in our case study of a [Texas driver crash in New York no-fault](/scenarios/texas-driver-crash-in-new-york-no-fault/) jurisdiction.
Proof of Insurance: What Counts in California

California Vehicle Code section 16028 requires drivers to show evidence of financial responsibility when a police officer asks and after any collision. An insurance ID card, on paper or on your phone, is what nearly everyone uses. Separately, insurers must electronically report private-passenger vehicle coverage to the DMV under Vehicle Code section 16058, which is how the DMV knows the moment a policy is cancelled. Forgetting the card at a traffic stop has its own penalties, covered in [what happens if you can't show proof of insurance in California](/qa/california-no-proof-of-insurance-ticket/), and a crash triggers a separate DMV report explained in [do you have to report an accident to the California DMV](/qa/california-sr1-accident-report/). Drivers on tight budgets can stay legal through the state's genuine [California Low Cost Auto Insurance Program](/learn/california-low-cost-auto-insurance-program/). If you are selling a car, storing one, or switching insurers, the order of operations matters, and our [California evidence of liability insurance](/learn/california-evidence-of-liability-insurance/) walkthrough explains how to switch without triggering a suspension notice.
Florida: Real State Programs vs 'Program' Advertising

Search 'Florida compliant drivers program' and you will find ads promising a special state rate for drivers with clean records. No Florida agency runs a program by that name. The phrase is used by lead-generation sites that collect your details and sell them to agents. The genuine savings routes are less exciting but real: the state-approved mature driver course for drivers 55 and older (authorized by Florida Statutes section 627.0652, with a discount that typically lasts three years), safe-driver rating, and usage-based telematics. Our [Florida compliant drivers program](/learn/florida-compliant-drivers-program/) breakdown shows how to tell an insurer quote from a lead form. For the legal baseline, start with [what is the minimum car insurance required in Florida](/qa/florida-minimum-car-insurance-requirements/), learn the deadlines that cut benefits in [Florida PIP insurance explained](/learn/florida-pip-insurance-explained/), see how drivers 55+ claim the [Florida mature driver insurance discount](/learn/florida-mature-driver-insurance-discount/), and know the fees in [what happens if car insurance lapses in Florida](/qa/what-happens-if-car-insurance-lapses-in-florida/).

content.title: Why Fake 'Government Program' Ads Matter
content.text: In 2025 the Federal Trade Commission settled with lead generator MediaAlpha for $45 million over health insurance ads that faked an affiliation with the government. The same playbook appears in auto insurance. A real state program never needs your Social Security number on a landing page to 'check eligibility'.
When the State Makes Your Insurer Vouch for You: SR-22 and FR-44

After certain violations, carrying insurance is no longer enough; your insurer has to file a certificate with the state confirming you are covered and promising to notify the state if the policy ends. That certificate is the [SR-22](/qa/can-you-get-auto-insurance-with-a-suspended-license/). Florida adds a second, stricter version, the FR-44, for DUI convictions, with limits of 100/300/50 that must be held for at least three years. The two are often confused, so we answer the difference directly in [SR-22 vs FR-44: what is the difference](/qa/sr22-vs-fr44-difference/). Because these filings sit on top of a policy, the size of your [premium](/glossary/premium/) is driven by the violation, not the paperwork.
RVs: Where Auto Rules and Home-Style Coverage Meet

A motorhome is a motor vehicle, so in California it needs the same 30/60/15 liability as a sedan. A travel trailer or fifth wheel has no stand-alone insurance mandate; your tow vehicle's liability generally extends to it while it is hitched, but nothing pays for damage to the trailer itself unless you buy physical damage coverage. Full-time RVers need something closer to a homeowners policy on wheels. All of it is covered in our [California RV insurance guide](/learn/california-rv-insurance/), including how [comprehensive vs collision](/compare/comprehensive-vs-collision/) choices change when the vehicle is also your living room. If you tow, read [does car insurance cover a travel trailer](/qa/does-car-insurance-cover-travel-trailer/); if you live on the road, read [full-time RV insurance](/learn/full-time-rv-insurance/).
The Other Compliance Bill California Homebuyers Meet: PMI

Compliance is not only a driving issue. Lenders impose their own insurance requirements, and the most expensive one for California buyers is private mortgage insurance on conventional loans with less than 20% down. Freddie Mac estimates PMI at roughly $30 to $70 a month for every $100,000 borrowed, and California loan sizes magnify that. Federal law sets clear points at which it must come off. Read [California private mortgage insurance](/learn/california-private-mortgage-insurance/) for the cancellation rules and the state's CalHFA assistance programs, and [PMI vs FHA MIP](/compare/pmi-vs-fha-mip/) if you are deciding between loan types.
Your Compliance Checklist

items: **Check your declarations page** against the current state minimum. Our guide on [how to read an insurance policy](/learn/how-to-read-an-insurance-policy/) shows where the limits sit.
**Keep digital proof on your phone** and a paper card in the glovebox for dead-battery days.
**Never cancel before replacing.** Start the new policy first, then cancel the old one, so the state's database never sees a gap.

**Surrender or store properly.** In Florida, surrender the plate before cancelling coverage on a car you no longer use; in California, use planned non-operation status rather than simply letting coverage lapse.
**Treat 'state program' ads with suspicion** unless the URL ends in .gov or the ad names a licensed insurer.
**If you were ordered to file an SR-22 or FR-44**, set a calendar reminder for the end date and confirm with the state before dropping the filing. See [SR-22 vs FR-44](/qa/sr22-vs-fr44-difference/).
**Insure the RV separately** if you own one, and confirm whether your trailer is covered while unhitched. See [California RV insurance](/learn/california-rv-insurance/).
